facts.text: - Reporting entity: OPENLANE, Inc., a Delaware registrant, common stock listed as OPLN on the New York Stock Exchange (10-Q Q3 page:1 "Common Stock, par value $0.01 per share OPLN New York Stock Exchange"). The context leaves borrower, parent and guarantor fields blank. The filings identify the company itself as borrower under the Credit Agreement, with a Canadian subsidiary as borrower under the Canadian facility (10-Q Q3 page:18 "ADESA Auctions Canada Corporation, a subsidiary of the Company"). No parent entity is named in the sources read; that is not evidence that none exists above the registrant. - Term loan and revolvers: the 2025 Incremental Term Loans, the Revolving Credit Facility and the Canadian Revolving Credit Facility are obligations under the Credit Agreement. Quote: 10-Q Q3 page:18 "guaranteed by certain of our domestic subsidiaries". The Canadian facility has a Canadian Borrower and its own guarantor set (10-Q Q3 page:20). The names of the guarantors are not in the text read (gap G2). - Finance segment funding: AFC sells receivables to AFC Funding Corporation, a bankruptcy remote special purpose subsidiary that is consolidated, and AFCI has a separate Canadian facility. Quote: 10-Q Q3 page:15 "wholly-owned, bankruptcy remote, consolidated, special purpose subsidiary". The receivables sold are accounted for as secured borrowings, so the obligations appear as "Obligations collateralized by finance receivables" on the balance sheet (10-Q Q3 page:3), a liability line separate from "Long-term debt". The two lines are printed side by side: 10-Q Q3 page:17 "Total debt $ 545.9 $ 550.0" for the debt table and 10-Q Q3 page:3 "Obligations collateralized by finance receivables 2,064.1 1,758.3" for the securitization obligations. This is a perimeter distinction CP-1 and CP-2 must carry. - Preferred equity: Series A convertible preferred stock held by affiliates of Apax and Periphas was partly repurchased in October 2025 and the rest converted to common stock in May 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:22). It is no longer outstanding at the latest balance sheet date (10-Q Q3 page:23). - Non-GAAP perimeter: Adjusted EBITDA in the decks and 10-Qs is a company measure that deducts securitization interest in the Finance segment (Deck Q3 page:6 "Securitization interest"). Covenant EBITDA is defined separately in the Credit Agreement (10-Q Q3 page:54). The two definitions differ and the sources do not reconcile them.

facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: audited FY2025 statements and the three 2026 interim filings give a filed foundation for FY2025 and for the first, second and third quarters of 2026 and the nine months, with covenant and liquidity text in each filing. The nine months and the quarter are separate periods and must stay separate. - Strongest contrary evidence: the Finance segment funds itself through receivable securitizations that the company accounts for as secured borrowings. The 10-Q Q3 states the committed U.S. liquidity and the Canadian facility size and that the agreements incorporate the Credit Agreement financial covenants (10-Q Q3 page:16 "The securitization agreements also incorporate the financial covenants of our Credit Agreement"). A consumer that reads only "Long-term debt" would omit the larger collateralized obligations. - Source risk mechanism: the covenant ratio disclosed in the filings is a senior secured test that applies only on quarters in which loans under the revolvers are outstanding (10-Q Q3 page:54 "on which any loans under the Revolving Credit Facilities are outstanding"). The filing reports no borrowings on the revolvers (10-Q Q3 page:20 "there were no borrowings on the Revolving Credit Facilities"), and the ratio definition rests on Credit Agreement text that is not supplied. Any headroom conclusion therefore depends on a document outside the pack, and whether the test applies in a given quarter is a legal reading this module does not make. - Version risk: the annual report gave a December 31, 2025 collateral figure that the 2026 10-Qs describe as an error and correct (10-Q Q3 page:16 "reflects the correction of an error from the $2,803.5 million previously disclosed in the 2025 Form 10-K"). The annual report remains the audited source for everything else, and the earlier figure sits at 10-K FY2025 page:77 and page:119. - What cannot proceed: legal reading of the Credit Agreement and securitization agreements, guarantor-level analysis, rating or market-based work. - Next evidence action: supply the Credit Agreement and its amendments (Exhibits 10.1a to 10.1d in the 10-Q Q3 exhibit index, including the Third Amendment dated June 30, 2026, whose terms the debt note does not describe), the Tenth Amended and Restated Receivables Purchase Agreement and its 2026 amendments (Exhibits 10.10a to 10.10c) and the Canadian Receivables Purchase Agreement and its amendments (Exhibits 10.11a to 10.11e), and Exhibit 21.1 of the annual report; confirm whether any 8-K after November 4, 2026 exists.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported base is complete enough for credit work on OPENLANE, Inc.: audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements, three unaudited 2026 interim filings through September 30, 2026, and a company-printed LTM reconciliation at each 2026 quarter-end that matches the sum of quarters. The base separates three claims that a single leverage number would blur. First, corporate debt: one term loan of 545.9 and revolvers with no borrowings. Second, securitization obligations of 2,084.4 gross that fund the Finance segment's floorplan receivables and are accounted for as secured borrowings. Third, equity-like claims, namely the Series A preferred that was fully converted in May 2026. Company Adjusted EBITDA deducts securitization interest, so ratios on it use corporate debt only; ratios on unadjusted EBITDA use total cash interest. Both bases are shown and not mixed. All ratios below are the analyst's calculations from printed inputs and differ from the covenant ratio the company reports, whose definition rests on an agreement that is not supplied. Restrictions carried forward: covenant definitions, securitization capacity and the Third Amendment to the Credit Agreement cannot be verified from the pack.

facts.label: Securitization and funding of the Finance segment
facts.text: AFC sells most U.S. dollar receivables on a revolving basis, without recourse, to AFC Funding Corporation. The sales are accounted for as secured borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:15 "The receivables sold pursuant to both the U.S. and Canadian securitization agreements are accounted for as secured borrowings"). Receivables serving as security were 2,786.7 at September 30, 2026 against gross obligations of 2,084.4, and a cash reserve of 1 or 3 percent of the obligations is also held (10-Q Q3 page:16). The 10-K gave 2,803.5 for December 31, 2025 collateral (10-K FY2025 page:77); the 2026 10-Qs state a corrected 2,448.2 for the same date. This module uses 2,448.2 for December 31, 2025 and treats 2,803.5 as superseded for that single line.

facts.label: Securitization and funding of the Finance segment
facts.text: The filing states that approximately 70% to 75% of the receivable portfolio is funded through the securitization facilities, the remainder from cash on hand and working capital (10-Q Q3 page:60 "approximately 70% to 75% of AFC’s finance receivables portfolio is funded through its securitization facilities"). The calculated share at September 30, 2026 is 75.4% (2,084.4 over total receivables managed of 2,763.5), and 73.1% at December 31, 2025. The September 2026 amendments extended both facilities from January 31, 2028 to January 31, 2030 and yielded about 58 of incremental borrowing (10-Q Q3 page:57). AFC and the securitization vehicles must meet covenants on debt incurrence, minimum tangible net worth and portfolio performance, and the agreements incorporate the Credit Agreement financial covenants; the tangible net worth level is Not supplied, and tangible parent equity was 526.7 at September 30, 2026 against 534.4 at December 31, 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:42).

facts.label: Covenants
facts.text: The calculated net debt over Adjusted EBITDA (0.79 at LTM Q3 2026) is below the reported 0.9 at the same date. The difference is a definition difference, not an error: the covenant uses Consolidated Total Debt and Consolidated EBITDA as defined in the Credit Agreement, with Unrestricted Cash as defined there, and the company Adjusted EBITDA is its own non-GAAP measure. The covenant EBITDA adds back items such as stock-based compensation and restructuring-type costs (10-Q Q3 page:54) and the pack does not reconcile the two measures.

facts.label: Earnings quality: the bridge from EBITDA to Adjusted EBITDA
facts.text: For LTM Q3 2026, EBITDA of 451.5 is reduced by net deductions of 68.8 to reach Adjusted EBITDA of 382.7 (10-Q Q3 page:59). The largest single item is the deduction for securitization interest of 95.9. That deduction is partly offset by non-cash stock-based compensation of 30.8. The first quarter of 2026 also carries a deduction of 15.9 for the Impact of Canadian DST related to prior years (10-Q Q3 page:59), which removes a one-time benefit from Adjusted EBITDA. New add-back lines appear in Q3 2026: transaction-related costs of 1.7 and a loss on extinguishment of debt of 0.7 (10-Q Q3 page:58). Because Adjusted EBITDA is stated after securitization interest, it is a corporate-level measure for leverage. It is not comparable with unadjusted EBITDA, and the interest-cover table keeps the two bases apart.

facts.label: Interpretation for credit
facts.text: 1. Corporate leverage is low on the company measure. Debt of 545.9 is covered 1.43 times by LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 382.7, down from 1.65 at FY2025 because LTM Adjusted EBITDA is higher (382.7 against 332.6) while principal debt is about the same (545.9 against 550.0). At FY2024 the figure was 0.79, before the October 2025 term loan funded the preferred repurchase. 2. The all-in funded picture is much larger. Securitization obligations of 2,084.4 gross are not secured by the general assets of the company and are carried against 2,763.5 of receivables managed. Their risk is the quality and growth of floorplan receivables, not corporate leverage; delinquent receivables were 0.6% of receivables managed against 0.3% a year earlier. 3. Interest burden has stepped up. Corporate interest, net of interest income, is 37.3 for LTM Q3 2026 against 14.9 for FY2025 and 21.2 at LTM Q1 2026, as the term loan took effect in the fourth quarter of 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:35). Run-rate cover on Adjusted EBITDA is therefore better read as 10.26 than as the 22.32 for FY2025. 4. Liquidity is adequate. Cash of 244.9 and undrawn revolver availability of 405.3 total 650.2 against annual term-loan amortization of 5.5 and no maturity before June 23, 2028. The securitization facilities are committed to January 31, 2030. 5. Share repurchases are rising and compete with deleveraging. The buyback program was enlarged to 400 in October 2026, and 9M 2026 repurchases were 91.5. The Credit Agreement limits dividends and distributions, but baskets are Not supplied.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: OPENLANE, Inc. is a stand-alone public company, formerly KAR Auction Services, that runs a digital wholesale used-vehicle marketplace in the United States, Canada and Europe and, through AFC, a short-term floorplan lender to independent dealers. Revenue is mostly fees on volume, with a small share of vehicles bought and resold; the lender adds interest and fees, funded mainly by receivable securitizations that the CP-1 handoff shows outside the corporate debt figure. The creditor-relevant transaction record is a sequence of capital-structure steps rather than an acquisition or a buyout: a term loan drawn in October 2025 to repurchase most of the Series A preferred stock held by affiliates of Apax and Periphas, the conversion of the rest into common stock in May 2026, securitization extensions to January 2030 in September 2026, and a larger share repurchase program in October 2026. No sponsor-led buyout, merger or pending acquisition is described in the sources, and the context names no sponsor. Operationally, the quarter shows strong volume growth led by commercial consignors and a lower fee yield, which makes revenue durability depend on a small number of large consignment relationships and on off-lease supply that management expects to grow. The main restrictions on this view are that the executed credit and securitization agreements are not supplied, that the present holdings and board rights of the former preferred holders are not stated after the conversion and the August 2026 secondary offering, and that the nature of the new Q3 2026 transaction-related costs is not explained.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On October 8, 2025 the company entered into a Second Amendment to its Credit Agreement that added incremental term loans of 550.0, due October 2032, priced at Adjusted Term SOFR plus 2.50%, issued at a discount of 2.7 with about 6.1 of debt issuance costs capitalized, and repayable in quarterly installments of 0.25% of the original principal that began on March 31, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:18). The proceeds were used to finance the repurchase of Series A preferred stock and related fees and expenses. In October 2025 the company repurchased 334,028 Series A shares from affiliates of Apax and Periphas for about 559.3, recorded a deemed dividend of about 242.2 against the carrying amount, and later paid 5.6 of excise tax in the second quarter of 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:22). In May 2026 the holders elected to convert the remaining 300,277 Series A shares into 17,103,116 shares of common stock, a non-cash transaction, and the series was eliminated (10-Q Q3 page:22 and page:23). The earlier debt events are a January 2024 First Amendment that added a C$175 million Canadian revolver, the June 2025 repayment at maturity of the 5.125% senior notes with 210.0 of cash, and the 2023 Credit Agreement with a $325 million revolver due June 23, 2028 (10-Q Q3 page:18; 10-K FY2025 page:4 and page:75). In September 2026 the U.S. securitization facility (committed liquidity of 2.0 billion) and the Canadian facility (C$500 million) were each extended from January 31, 2028 to January 31, 2030, with about 12.5 of costs capitalized, a 0.7 pretax loss on extinguishment recorded, and about 58 of incremental borrowing (10-Q Q3 page:15, page:56 and page:57). The exhibit index lists a Third Amendment to the Credit Agreement dated June 30, 2026 and a Second Amendment to the Tenth Amended and Restated Receivables Purchase Agreement dated September 25, 2026; the debt note does not describe the Third Amendment, so its terms are Not supplied (10-Q Q3 page:68 and page:69). The debt stack, maturities and leverage are in the CP-1 handoff and are not repeated. No acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction, new bond issue or rating event is described in the sources up to November 4, 2026. After the quarter, in October 2026, the board raised the share repurchase program from 250 to 400 and extended it to December 31, 2027, and 306,334 shares were repurchased for 11.1 (10-Q Q3 page:27). On November 4, 2026 management raised its 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to 390 to 400 from 385 to 400, which is a management claim and not a filed fact (Deck Q3 page:5).

citations.quote: On October 8, 2025 the company entered into a Second Amendment to its Credit Agreement that added incremental term loans of 550.0, due October 2032, priced at Adjusted Term SOFR plus 2.50%, issued at a discount of 2.7 with about 6.1 of debt issuance costs capitalized, and repayable in quarterly installments of 0.25% of the original principal that began on March 31, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:18). The proceeds were used to finance the repurchase of Series A preferred stock and related fees and expenses. In October 2025 the company repurchased 334,028 Series A shares from affiliates of Apax and Periphas for about 559.3, recorded a deemed dividend of about 242.2 against the carrying amount, and later paid 5.6 of excise tax in the second quarter of 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:22). In May 2026 the holders elected to convert the remaining 300,277 Series A shares into 17,103,116 shares of common stock, a non-cash transaction, and the series was eliminated (10-Q Q3 page:22 and page:23). The earlier debt events are a January 2024 First Amendment that added a C$175 million Canadian revolver, the June 2025 repayment at maturity of the 5.125% senior notes with 210.0 of cash, and the 2023 Credit Agreement with a $325 million revolver due June 23, 2028 (10-Q Q3 page:18; 10-K FY2025 page:4 and page:75). In September 2026 the U.S. securitization facility (committed liquidity of 2.0 billion) and the Canadian facility (C$500 million) were each extended from January 31, 2028 to January 31, 2030, with about 12.5 of costs capitalized, a 0.7 pretax loss on extinguishment recorded, and about 58 of incremental borrowing (10-Q Q3 page:15, page:56 and page:57). The exhibit index lists a Third Amendment to the Credit Agreement dated June 30, 2026 and a Second Amendment to the Tenth Amended and Restated Receivables Purchase Agreement dated September 25, 2026; the debt note does not describe the Third Amendment, so its terms are Not supplied (10-Q Q3 page:68 and page:69). The debt stack, maturities and leverage are in the CP-1 handoff and are not repeated. No acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction, new bond issue or rating event is described in the sources up to November 4, 2026. After the quarter, in October 2026, the board raised the share repurchase program from 250 to 400 and extended it to December 31, 2027, and 306,334 shares were repurchased for 11.1 (10-Q Q3 page:27). On November 4, 2026 management raised its 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to 390 to 400 from 385 to 400, which is a management claim and not a filed fact (Deck Q3 page:5).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: OPENLANE, Inc. is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative issuer whose corporate credit profile is sound, but whose balance sheet is dominated by receivable-backed funding. Its strongest support is a single term loan of USD 545.9 million, undrawn revolvers and USD 650.2 million of liquidity, which put total debt at 1.43x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million [CP-1 leverage and liquidity tables]. Its weakest point is that USD 2,084.4 million of securitization obligations sit outside that ratio and fund a dealer-credit book whose losses follow wholesale vehicle prices, while commercial volume growth rests on consignors who can leave on notice [CP-1A credit translations]. The outcome turns on floorplan credit quality, continued access to the securitization facilities committed to January 31, 2030, and covenant terms that cannot be checked.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The corporate capital structure is simple and lightly levered: one secured term loan, revolvers with no borrowings and no maturity before June 23, 2028 other than USD 5.5 million of annual amortization [CP-1 debt stack; Documentary Fact]. Liquidity of USD 650.2 million and reported covenant headroom of 2.6x on a 3.5x test give room to absorb a downturn before the revolver is needed [CP-1 liquidity and covenants tables; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. The securitization facilities were extended by two years to January 31, 2030 in September 2026 [CP-1A timeline; Documentary Fact]. Customer exposure is spread, since no single customer was 10% or more of revenue and AFC has no dealer above 2.5% of its portfolio [CP-1A company and operating model; Documentary Fact]. The conversion of the remaining Series A preferred in May 2026 removed a senior equity claim with a 7% cash dividend and class vote rights [CP-1A ownership and control; Documentary Fact].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Corporate creditors rank behind a bankruptcy-remote structure for the best collateral: the receivables are sold to a consolidated special purpose subsidiary, and the facilities are not secured by the general assets of the company, so the term loan's claim on the Finance book is to the value left after the securitization obligations; whether the AFC Funding Corporation shares are pledged to the term-loan lenders is not stated [CP-1 securitization section; Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the mechanic]. After a termination event under the U.S. facility the banks may cause the stock of AFC Funding Corporation to be transferred to them, although as a practical matter the bank facility would look to liquidation of the receivables as its primary remedy (10-Q Q3 page:57 "the banks may, and could, cause the stock of AFC Funding Corporation to be transferred to the bank facility"), a loss-of-control mechanic that the handoffs do not carry. The Finance book is credit sensitive: delinquent receivables were 0.6% of receivables managed against 0.3% a year earlier, and a fall in wholesale used-vehicle prices would raise losses if dealers cannot meet obligations [CP-1A company and operating model; Documentary Fact]. Revenue durability is only moderate, because customers make no binding volume commitments and many agreements can be ended for convenience, and the Q3 2026 commercial growth leaned on onboarding a new private label customer [CP-1A credit translations; Documentary Fact]. Earnings quality needs care: nine-month 2026 Marketplace gross profit includes a USD 20.2 million Canadian tax reversal benefit, of which USD 15.9 million relates to prior periods and is removed from Adjusted EBITDA, while the USD 4.3 million current-period part (10-Q Q3 page:46) is not [CP-1A company and operating model; CP-1 earnings quality; Documentary Fact]. Floating-rate term debt is not hedged: the company states it does not use interest rate contracts (10-K FY2025 page:88 "We do not currently use interest rate contracts to manage our exposure to interest rate changes"), which is a point not carried by the handoffs [Documentary Fact]. Unverifiable items include covenant EBITDA definitions, the Third Amendment of June 30, 2026, the share of the company still held by former preferred holders, and the nature of USD 1.7 million of Q3 2026 transaction-related costs [CP-1A gaps; Insufficient Information].

citations.quote: Weaknesses. Corporate creditors rank behind a bankruptcy-remote structure for the best collateral: the receivables are sold to a consolidated special purpose subsidiary, and the facilities are not secured by the general assets of the company, so the term loan's claim on the Finance book is to the value left after the securitization obligations; whether the AFC Funding Corporation shares are pledged to the term-loan lenders is not stated [CP-1 securitization section; Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the mechanic]. After a termination event under the U.S. facility the banks may cause the stock of AFC Funding Corporation to be transferred to them, although as a practical matter the bank facility would look to liquidation of the receivables as its primary remedy (10-Q Q3 page:57 "the banks may, and could, cause the stock of AFC Funding Corporation to be transferred to the bank facility"), a loss-of-control mechanic that the handoffs do not carry. The Finance book is credit sensitive: delinquent receivables were 0.6% of receivables managed against 0.3% a year earlier, and a fall in wholesale used-vehicle prices would raise losses if dealers cannot meet obligations [CP-1A company and operating model; Documentary Fact]. Revenue durability is only moderate, because customers make no binding volume commitments and many agreements can be ended for convenience, and the Q3 2026 commercial growth leaned on onboarding a new private label customer [CP-1A credit translations; Documentary Fact]. Earnings quality needs care: nine-month 2026 Marketplace gross profit includes a USD 20.2 million Canadian tax reversal benefit, of which USD 15.9 million relates to prior periods and is removed from Adjusted EBITDA, while the USD 4.3 million current-period part (10-Q Q3 page:46) is not [CP-1A company and operating model; CP-1 earnings quality; Documentary Fact]. Floating-rate term debt is not hedged: the company states it does not use interest rate contracts (10-K FY2025 page:88 "We do not currently use interest rate contracts to manage our exposure to interest rate changes"), which is a point not carried by the handoffs [Documentary Fact]. Unverifiable items include covenant EBITDA definitions, the Third Amendment of June 30, 2026, the share of the company still held by former preferred holders, and the nature of USD 1.7 million of Q3 2026 transaction-related costs [CP-1A gaps; Insufficient Information].

facts.label: Credit thesis
facts.text: OPENLANE, Inc. is a lightly levered, liquid corporate borrower whose creditworthiness is driven less by its USD 545.9 million of term debt than by the credit quality and continued securitization funding of a dealer-finance book of USD 2,763.5 million of receivables managed and by the durability of commercial consignment volume.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: One new calculation is made here. Debt service cover on corporate obligations for LTM Q3 2026: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million divided by the sum of LTM interest expense net of interest income of USD 37.3 million and annual term-loan amortization of USD 5.5 million, which is USD 42.8 million, gives 8.94x [CP-1 financials table and maturity schedule]. It is a corporate-level measure, because Adjusted EBITDA is after securitization interest. All other figures are quoted from the CP-1 handoff and are not recomputed. The term-loan balance of USD 512.9 million in 2032 is the CP-1 schedule figure of 512.875, rounded.

### Perimeter and instrument roles

- Reporting entity: OPENLANE, Inc., a Delaware registrant, common stock listed as OPLN on the New York Stock Exchange (10-Q Q3 page:1 "Common Stock, par value $0.01 per share OPLN New York Stock Exchange"). The context leaves borrower, parent and guarantor fields blank. The filings identify the company itself as borrower under the Credit Agreement, with a Canadian subsidiary as borrower under the Canadian facility (10-Q Q3 page:18 "ADESA Auctions Canada Corporation, a subsidiary of the Company"). No parent entity is named in the sources read; that is not evidence that none exists above the registrant.

- Term loan and revolvers: the 2025 Incremental Term Loans, the Revolving Credit Facility and the Canadian Revolving Credit Facility are obligations under the Credit Agreement. Quote: 10-Q Q3 page:18 "guaranteed by certain of our domestic subsidiaries". The Canadian facility has a Canadian Borrower and its own guarantor set (10-Q Q3 page:20). The names of the guarantors are not in the text read (gap G2).

- Finance segment funding: AFC sells receivables to AFC Funding Corporation, a bankruptcy remote special purpose subsidiary that is consolidated, and AFCI has a separate Canadian facility. ### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: audited FY2025 statements and the three 2026 interim filings give a filed foundation for FY2025 and for the first, second and third quarters of 2026 and the nine months, with covenant and liquidity text in each filing. The nine months and the quarter are separate periods and must stay separate.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the Finance segment funds itself through receivable securitizations that the company accounts for as secured borrowings. The 10-Q Q3 states the committed U.S. liquidity and the Canadian facility size and that the agreements incorporate the Credit Agreement financial covenants (10-Q Q3 page:16 "The securitization agreements also incorporate the financial covenants of our Credit Agreement"). A consumer that reads only "Long-term debt" would omit the larger collateralized obligations.

- Source risk mechanism: the covenant ratio disclosed in the filings is a senior secured test that applies only on quarters in which loans under the revolvers are outstanding (10-Q Q3 page:54 "on which any loans under the Revolving Credit Facilities are outstanding"). The filing reports no borrowings on the revolvers (10-Q Q3 page:20 "there were no borrowings on the Revolving Credit Facilities"), and the ratio definition rests on Credit Agreement text that is not supplied. Any headroom conclusion therefore depends on a document outside the pack, and whether the test applies in a given quarter is a legal reading this module does not make.

- Version risk: the annual report gave a December 31, 2025 collateral figure that the 2026 10-Qs describe as an error and correct (10-Q Q3 page:16 "reflects the correction of an error from the $2,803.5 million previously disclosed in the 2025 Form 10-K"). - What cannot proceed: legal reading of the Credit Agreement and securitization agreements, guarantor-level analysis, rating or market-based work.

- Next evidence action: supply the Credit Agreement and its amendments (Exhibits 10.1a to 10.1d in the 10-Q Q3 exhibit index, including the Third Amendment dated June 30, 2026, whose terms the debt note does not describe), the Tenth Amended and Restated Receivables Purchase Agreement and its 2026 amendments (Exhibits 10.10a to 10.10c) and the Canadian Receivables Purchase Agreement and its amendments (Exhibits 10.11a to 10.11e), and Exhibit 21.1 of the annual report; confirm whether any 8-K after November 4, 2026 exists.

### Securitization and funding of the Finance segment

AFC sells most U.S. dollar receivables on a revolving basis, without recourse, to AFC Funding Corporation. The sales are accounted for as secured borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:15 "The receivables sold pursuant to both the U.S. and Canadian securitization agreements are accounted for as secured borrowings"). Receivables serving as security were 2,786.7 at September 30, 2026 against gross obligations of 2,084.4, and a cash reserve of 1 or 3 percent of the obligations is also held (10-Q Q3 page:16). The 10-K gave 2,803.5 for December 31, 2025 collateral (10-K FY2025 page:77); the 2026 10-Qs state a corrected 2,448.2 for the same date. This module uses 2,448.2 for December 31, 2025 and treats 2,803.5 as superseded for that single line.

The filing states that approximately 70% to 75% of the receivable portfolio is funded through the securitization facilities, the remainder from cash on hand and working capital (10-Q Q3 page:60 "approximately 70% to 75% of AFC’s finance receivables portfolio is funded through its securitization facilities"). The calculated share at September 30, 2026 is 75.4% (2,084.4 over total receivables managed of 2,763.5), and 73.1% at December 31, 2025. The September 2026 amendments extended both facilities from January 31, 2028 to January 31, 2030 and yielded about 58 of incremental borrowing (10-Q Q3 page:57). AFC and the securitization vehicles must meet covenants on debt incurrence, minimum tangible net worth and portfolio performance, and the agreements incorporate the Credit Agreement financial covenants; the tangible net worth level is Not supplied, and tangible parent equity was 526.7 at September 30, 2026 against 534.4 at December 31, 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:42).

The calculated net debt over Adjusted EBITDA (0.79 at LTM Q3 2026) is below the reported 0.9 at the same date. The difference is a definition difference, not an error: the covenant uses Consolidated Total Debt and Consolidated EBITDA as defined in the Credit Agreement, with Unrestricted Cash as defined there, and the company Adjusted EBITDA is its own non-GAAP measure. The covenant EBITDA adds back items such as stock-based compensation and restructuring-type costs (10-Q Q3 page:54) and the pack does not reconcile the two measures.
### Earnings quality: the bridge from EBITDA to Adjusted EBITDA

For LTM Q3 2026, EBITDA of 451.5 is reduced by net deductions of 68.8 to reach Adjusted EBITDA of 382.7 (10-Q Q3 page:59). The largest single item is the deduction for securitization interest of 95.9. That deduction is partly offset by non-cash stock-based compensation of 30.8. The first quarter of 2026 also carries a deduction of 15.9 for the Impact of Canadian DST related to prior years (10-Q Q3 page:59), which removes a one-time benefit from Adjusted EBITDA. New add-back lines appear in Q3 2026: transaction-related costs of 1.7 and a loss on extinguishment of debt of 0.7 (10-Q Q3 page:58). Because Adjusted EBITDA is stated after securitization interest, it is a corporate-level measure for leverage. It is not comparable with unadjusted EBITDA, and the interest-cover table keeps the two bases apart.

The Finance segment's Adjusted EBITDA is after its securitization interest. Finance revenue was 114.7 in Q3 2026 against 109.0 in Q3 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:40), the annualized provision for credit losses was 1.1% of average receivables managed against 1.6%, and delinquent receivables were 0.6% of total receivables managed against 0.3% (10-Q Q3 page:40).
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow was 309.5 for 9M 2026 against 266.4 for 9M 2025, and free cash flow, after capital purchases of 40.7 in each period, was 268.8 against 225.7. The finance receivables book is funded outside operating cash flow: receivables growth is in investing activities (367.6 for 9M 2026) and the matching increase in securitization obligations is in financing activities (322.9). The calculated free cash flow after both changes is 224.1 for 9M 2026 and 175.4 for 9M 2025. Common stock repurchases including excise taxes were 91.5 for 9M 2026 against 35.8 for 9M 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:5). The October 2025 Series A repurchase of approximately 559.3 was funded primarily with the 550.0 of term loans (10-K FY2025 page:122; 10-Q Q3 page:22). Q3 2026 buybacks were 1,237,828 shares at an average of 35.23 including 727,590 shares bought from the underwriter of an Apax secondary offering in August 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:66).
### Latest quarter and events to the cutoff

- September 2026: AFC and AFC Funding Corporation signed the 2026 Second Amendment and AFCI signed Amendment No. 4, extending both facilities to January 31, 2030. Capitalized costs were about 10.7 and 1.8, a loss on extinguishment of debt of 0.7 was recorded, and the amendments yielded about 58 of incremental borrowing (10-Q Q3 page:15 and page:57).
- June 30, 2026: a Third Amendment to the Credit Agreement is listed in the exhibit index (10-Q Q3 page:68). Its terms are not described in the debt note and are Not supplied.
- May 2026: the remaining Series A preferred stock (300,277 shares) converted into 17,103,116 shares of common stock, a non-cash transaction (10-Q Q3 page:22).

- October 2026 (subsequent event): the board raised the share repurchase program from 250 to 400 and extended it to December 31, 2027; 306,334 shares were repurchased for 11.1 in October 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:27).
- November 4, 2026 guidance: Adjusted EBITDA of 390 to 400 and capital expenditures of 55 to 60 for 2026, a management claim (Deck Q3 page:5).

- The Q3 2026 10-Q describes no corporate debt issuance or repayment beyond the scheduled term-loan installments, and the word waiver does not appear in it. Nothing after November 4, 2026 is supplied.
### Interpretation for credit

1. Corporate leverage is low on the company measure. Debt of 545.9 is covered 1.43 times by LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 382.7, down from 1.65 at FY2025 because LTM Adjusted EBITDA is higher (382.7 against 332.6) while principal debt is about the same (545.9 against 550.0). At FY2024 the figure was 0.79, before the October 2025 term loan funded the preferred repurchase.

2. The all-in funded picture is much larger. Securitization obligations of 2,084.4 gross are not secured by the general assets of the company and are carried against 2,763.5 of receivables managed. Their risk is the quality and growth of floorplan receivables, not corporate leverage; delinquent receivables were 0.6% of receivables managed against 0.3% a year earlier.

3. Interest burden has stepped up. Corporate interest, net of interest income, is 37.3 for LTM Q3 2026 against 14.9 for FY2025 and 21.2 at LTM Q1 2026, as the term loan took effect in the fourth quarter of 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:35). Run-rate cover on Adjusted EBITDA is therefore better read as 10.26 than as the 22.32 for FY2025.

4. Liquidity is adequate. Cash of 244.9 and undrawn revolver availability of 405.3 total 650.2 against annual term-loan amortization of 5.5 and no maturity before June 23, 2028. The securitization facilities are committed to January 31, 2030.

5. Share repurchases are rising and compete with deleveraging. The buyback program was enlarged to 400 in October 2026, and 9M 2026 repurchases were 91.5. The Credit Agreement limits dividends and distributions, but baskets are Not supplied.

### Business and transaction view

OPENLANE, Inc. is a stand-alone public company, formerly KAR Auction Services, that runs a digital wholesale used-vehicle marketplace in the United States, Canada and Europe and, through AFC, a short-term floorplan lender to independent dealers. Revenue is mostly fees on volume, with a small share of vehicles bought and resold; the lender adds interest and fees, funded mainly by receivable securitizations that the CP-1 handoff shows outside the corporate debt figure. The creditor-relevant transaction record is a sequence of capital-structure steps rather than an acquisition or a buyout: a term loan drawn in October 2025 to repurchase most of the Series A preferred stock held by affiliates of Apax and Periphas, the conversion of the rest into common stock in May 2026, securitization extensions to January 2030 in September 2026, and a larger share repurchase program in October 2026. No sponsor-led buyout, merger or pending acquisition is described in the sources, and the context names no sponsor. Operationally, the quarter shows strong volume growth led by commercial consignors and a lower fee yield, which makes revenue durability depend on a small number of large consignment relationships and on off-lease supply that management expects to grow. The main restrictions on this view are that the executed credit and securitization agreements are not supplied, that the present holdings and board rights of the former preferred holders are not stated after the conversion and the August 2026 secondary offering, and that the nature of the new Q3 2026 transaction-related costs is not explained.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On October 8, 2025 the company entered into a Second Amendment to its Credit Agreement that added incremental term loans of 550.0, due October 2032, priced at Adjusted Term SOFR plus 2.50%, issued at a discount of 2.7 with about 6.1 of debt issuance costs capitalized, and repayable in quarterly installments of 0.25% of the original principal that began on March 31, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:18). The proceeds were used to finance the repurchase of Series A preferred stock and related fees and expenses. In October 2025 the company repurchased 334,028 Series A shares from affiliates of Apax and Periphas for about 559.3, recorded a deemed dividend of about 242.2 against the carrying amount, and later paid 5.6 of excise tax in the second quarter of 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:22). In May 2026 the holders elected to convert the remaining 300,277 Series A shares into 17,103,116 shares of common stock, a non-cash transaction, and the series was eliminated (10-Q Q3 page:22 and page:23). The earlier debt events are a January 2024 First Amendment that added a C$175 million Canadian revolver, the June 2025 repayment at maturity of the 5.125% senior notes with 210.0 of cash, and the 2023 Credit Agreement with a $325 million revolver due June 23, 2028 (10-Q Q3 page:18; 10-K FY2025 page:4 and page:75). In September 2026 the U.S. securitization facility (committed liquidity of 2.0 billion) and the Canadian facility (C$500 million) were each extended from January 31, 2028 to January 31, 2030, with about 12.5 of costs capitalized, a 0.7 pretax loss on extinguishment recorded, and about 58 of incremental borrowing (10-Q Q3 page:15, page:56 and page:57). The exhibit index lists a Third Amendment to the Credit Agreement dated June 30, 2026 and a Second Amendment to the Tenth Amended and Restated Receivables Purchase Agreement dated September 25, 2026; the debt note does not describe the Third Amendment, so its terms are Not supplied (10-Q Q3 page:68 and page:69). The debt stack, maturities and leverage are in the CP-1 handoff and are not repeated. No acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction, new bond issue or rating event is described in the sources up to November 4, 2026. After the quarter, in October 2026, the board raised the share repurchase program from 250 to 400 and extended it to December 31, 2027, and 306,334 shares were repurchased for 11.1 (10-Q Q3 page:27). On November 4, 2026 management raised its 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to 390 to 400 from 385 to 400, which is a management claim and not a filed fact (Deck Q3 page:5).

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| OPENLANE has a sound corporate credit profile, with total debt at 1.43x LTM Adjusted EBITDA and liquidity of USD 650.2 million, but most funding is receivable-backed securitization and its performance decides the credit. | Medium | The credit and securitization agreements are not supplied, so covenant terms and undrawn securitization capacity are unverified. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt is USD 545.9 million, one term loan with undrawn revolvers, against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million. | Corporate leverage is low, and the reported covenant ratio is 0.9x against a 3.5x maximum. | Medium |

| Securitization obligations are USD 2,084.4 million gross, outside the corporate debt figure. | The Finance book is funded largely by facilities not secured by the company's general assets, so its credit losses reach creditors through earnings and funding access. | High |

| Commercial volume growth of 46% in Q3 2026 falls to 17% excluding the latest customer. | Revenue visibility depends on consignors who can terminate for convenience, and fee yield is diluted. | Medium |
| Corporate net interest rose to USD 37.3 million LTM from USD 14.9 million in FY2025. | The October 2025 term loan raised fixed charges, though Adjusted EBITDA covers net interest 10.26x. | High |
### Credit view

OPENLANE, Inc. is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative issuer whose corporate credit profile is sound, but whose balance sheet is dominated by receivable-backed funding. Its strongest support is a single term loan of USD 545.9 million, undrawn revolvers and USD 650.2 million of liquidity, which put total debt at 1.43x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million [CP-1 leverage and liquidity tables]. Its weakest point is that USD 2,084.4 million of securitization obligations sit outside that ratio and fund a dealer-credit book whose losses follow wholesale vehicle prices, while commercial volume growth rests on consignors who can leave on notice [CP-1A credit translations]. The outcome turns on floorplan credit quality, continued access to the securitization facilities committed to January 31, 2030, and covenant terms that cannot be checked.
### Key findings

OPENLANE, Inc. carries low corporate leverage on the company measure: total debt of USD 545.9 million is 1.43x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, against 1.65x for FY2025 and 0.79x for FY2024, and net of cash it is 0.79x [CP-1 leverage table; Analyst Interpretation]. The step from FY2024 to FY2025 came from the USD 550.0 million term loan drawn in October 2025 to repurchase most of the Series A preferred stock [CP-1A transaction summary; Documentary Fact]. The company reports a covenant ratio of 0.9x at September 30, 2026 against a 3.5x maximum that applies on quarters when revolver loans are outstanding, and the revolvers have no borrowings [CP-1 covenants table; Documentary Fact].

The funded balance sheet is larger than the corporate debt figure. Securitization obligations are USD 2,084.4 million gross, or 75.4% of USD 2,763.5 million of receivables managed, against collateral coverage of 1.34x [CP-1 securitization section; Documentary Fact and calculation]. Company Adjusted EBITDA is stated after deducting securitization interest, so its leverage ratio is a corporate-level measure, and the cash-interest cover of 3.42x on unadjusted EBITDA is the comparable all-in view [CP-1 interest cover table; Analyst Interpretation].

Liquidity is ample against near-term obligations. Cash of USD 244.9 million and undrawn revolver availability of USD 405.3 million total USD 650.2 million, term-loan amortization is USD 5.5 million a year, and the next scheduled maturity beyond amortization is the revolvers on June 23, 2028, followed by a term-loan balance of USD 512.9 million due on October 8, 2032 on the CP-1 analyst schedule, which assumes installments on each quarter-end and no prepayment [CP-1 liquidity and maturity tables; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. The securitization facilities expire on January 31, 2030, which is the nearer refinancing event.

Cash generation is strong but flattered by classification. Free cash flow was USD 268.8 million for nine months 2026 and USD 379.6 million LTM, but receivable growth of USD 367.6 million sits in investing activities and was funded USD 322.9 million by securitization, leaving USD 224.1 million after both [CP-1 calculations; Documentary Fact and calculation].

The earnings base mixes two businesses. Marketplace is 78% of FY2025 revenue and Finance 22%, yet Finance is 48.3% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1A company and operating model; CP-1 segment view]. In Q3 2026 commercial vehicles sold rose 46%, or 17% excluding the latest commercial customer, while yield fell to 2.5% from 2.9% on mix [CP-1A company and operating model; Management Language for the 17%].

Capital allocation is shifting to shareholders. Repurchases were USD 91.5 million for nine months 2026 against USD 35.8 million, and the program was raised to USD 400 million in October 2026, with restricted-payment baskets not supplied [CP-1 cash flow quality; CP-1A governance table; Documentary Fact].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The corporate capital structure is simple and lightly levered: one secured term loan, revolvers with no borrowings and no maturity before June 23, 2028 other than USD 5.5 million of annual amortization [CP-1 debt stack; Documentary Fact]. Liquidity of USD 650.2 million and reported covenant headroom of 2.6x on a 3.5x test give room to absorb a downturn before the revolver is needed [CP-1 liquidity and covenants tables; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. The securitization facilities were extended by two years to January 31, 2030 in September 2026 [CP-1A timeline; Documentary Fact]. Customer exposure is spread, since no single customer was 10% or more of revenue and AFC has no dealer above 2.5% of its portfolio [CP-1A company and operating model; Documentary Fact]. The conversion of the remaining Series A preferred in May 2026 removed a senior equity claim with a 7% cash dividend and class vote rights [CP-1A ownership and control; Documentary Fact].

Weaknesses. Corporate creditors rank behind a bankruptcy-remote structure for the best collateral: the receivables are sold to a consolidated special purpose subsidiary, and the facilities are not secured by the general assets of the company, so the term loan's claim on the Finance book is to the value left after the securitization obligations; whether the AFC Funding Corporation shares are pledged to the term-loan lenders is not stated [CP-1 securitization section; Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the mechanic]. After a termination event under the U.S. facility the banks may cause the stock of AFC Funding Corporation to be transferred to them, although as a practical matter the bank facility would look to liquidation of the receivables as its primary remedy (10-Q Q3 page:57 "the banks may, and could, cause the stock of AFC Funding Corporation to be transferred to the bank facility"), a loss-of-control mechanic that the handoffs do not carry. The Finance book is credit sensitive: delinquent receivables were 0.6% of receivables managed against 0.3% a year earlier, and a fall in wholesale used-vehicle prices would raise losses if dealers cannot meet obligations [CP-1A company and operating model; Documentary Fact]. Revenue durability is only moderate, because customers make no binding volume commitments and many agreements can be ended for convenience, and the Q3 2026 commercial growth leaned on onboarding a new private label customer [CP-1A credit translations; Documentary Fact]. Earnings quality needs care: nine-month 2026 Marketplace gross profit includes a USD 20.2 million Canadian tax reversal benefit, of which USD 15.9 million relates to prior periods and is removed from Adjusted EBITDA, while the USD 4.3 million current-period part (10-Q Q3 page:46) is not [CP-1A company and operating model; CP-1 earnings quality; Documentary Fact]. Floating-rate term debt is not hedged: the company states it does not use interest rate contracts (10-K FY2025 page:88 "We do not currently use interest rate contracts to manage our exposure to interest rate changes"), which is a point not carried by the handoffs [Documentary Fact]. Unverifiable items include covenant EBITDA definitions, the Third Amendment of June 30, 2026, the share of the company still held by former preferred holders, and the nature of USD 1.7 million of Q3 2026 transaction-related costs [CP-1A gaps; Insufficient Information].
### Credit assessment

| Fundamental credit view | Sound corporate credit with low reported leverage and ample liquidity; credit outcome tied to the performance and funding of the Finance receivable book and to commercial consignment volume | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity and covenants tables; CP-1A company and operating model, ownership and control, credit translations |

| Limitation on confidence | Executed credit and securitization agreements, current holdings of the former preferred holders and facility-level securitization balances are not supplied; the CP-1A readiness for this module is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, not READY | Insufficient Information | Medium | CP-0 readiness view; CP-1A consumer readiness |
### Credit thesis

OPENLANE, Inc. is a lightly levered, liquid corporate borrower whose creditworthiness is driven less by its USD 545.9 million of term debt than by the credit quality and continued securitization funding of a dealer-finance book of USD 2,763.5 million of receivables managed and by the durability of commercial consignment volume.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Dealer credit and wholesale price cycle in Finance | A fall in used-vehicle prices or dealer demand lowers collateral value and raises defaults; delinquent receivables were 0.6% of receivables managed in Q3 2026 against 0.3% | Finance is 48.3% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA, so loss severity reduces earnings and could tighten securitization eligibility; monitor delinquency and provision rate | Material | CP-1A company and operating model; CP-1 segment view |

| Securitization funding access and structural position | Corporate creditors have no claim on securitized receivables beyond the residual, and termination events let banks take the AFC Funding Corporation stock; facilities are committed to January 31, 2030 | Refinancing and liquidity risk for the Finance book sits at the facilities; recovery for corporate creditors would depend on residual value, a mechanic only | Material | CP-1 securitization section; 10-Q Q3 page:57 |

| Commercial consignor concentration and yield dilution | Customers can terminate for convenience; growth leaned on a new customer; yield fell to 2.5% from 2.9% | Revenue visibility is moderate and fee income per vehicle is diluted by mix | Material | CP-1A company and operating model, credit translations |

| Higher fixed charges and unhedged floating rate | Corporate net interest was USD 37.3 million LTM against USD 14.9 million in FY2025; term loan floats on Adjusted Term SOFR plus 2.50% | Cover remains high at 10.26x on Adjusted EBITDA, but a rate rise or EBITDA fall reduces it | Minor | CP-1 financials table, debt stack |

| Capital returns ahead of deleveraging | Repurchases of USD 91.5 million for nine months 2026 and an enlarged program; basket limits not supplied | Leverage tolerance is untested above the current level; monitor distributions | Minor | CP-1 cash flow quality; CP-1A governance table |

| Unverified covenant definitions and amendments | Covenant EBITDA differs from company Adjusted EBITDA and the Third Amendment is undescribed | Headroom of 2.6x on reported terms cannot be tested independently | Material | CP-1 covenants table and gaps |
## Calculations

One new calculation is made here. Debt service cover on corporate obligations for LTM Q3 2026: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 382.7 million divided by the sum of LTM interest expense net of interest income of USD 37.3 million and annual term-loan amortization of USD 5.5 million, which is USD 42.8 million, gives 8.94x [CP-1 financials table and maturity schedule]. It is a corporate-level measure, because Adjusted EBITDA is after securitization interest. All other figures are quoted from the CP-1 handoff and are not recomputed. The term-loan balance of USD 512.9 million in 2032 is the CP-1 schedule figure of 512.875, rounded.
